question: The tube which grows out of pollen grain to reach the ovary, travels through the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pollen tube grows from the pollen grain and travels through the style to reach the ovary.
 
• The style is a slender stalk that connects the stigma to the ovary in the flower.
 
• The primary function of the style is to provide a pathway for the pollen tube to deliver sperm cells to the ovule.
 
• The growth of the pollen tube through the style is a crucial step in the fertilization process in flowering plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stigma**

 
 
• The stigma is the part of the pistil where pollen germinates.
 
• It is typically sticky, aiding in the capture of pollen grains.
 
 
 
• **Ovary**
 
 
• The ovary is the enlarged basal portion of the pistil where ovules are produced.
 
• After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit.
 
 
 
• **Anther**
 
 
• The anther is the part of a stamen that contains the pollen.
 
• It is typically located at the top of the filament.
 
 
 
• **Filament**
 
 
• The filament is the stalk that supports the anther in the stamen.
 
• It helps position the anther for effective pollen transfer.
